label: copy-phase input of e (fed-back copy of e), from the 3rd original position on
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the token fed back as input is the letter e, i.e. the model has just copied an e from original position >= 2 (recall_idx >= 3). It never fires on e during the original phase, at the delimiter, or on any other input token (only a handful of stray activations elsewhere). Magnitude grows with how late the copied e sits in the sequence: e copied from position 2 gives weak activations (about 0.1-0.5 of max), and the strongest activations (0.8-1.0) come from e at positions 5-7 of long sequences. e copied from positions 0-1 gives zero or tiny activations, and that is why the recall_idx >= 3 condition is there. It does not depend on the token being output next, on the previous token, or on the first token.

issues: None of the checks found a systematic problem. On the test split the predicate scores precision 0.990, recall 0.984, F1 0.987 and mass recall 0.998, which matches the reported scores.

The phase claims hold. The feature has 0 activations in the original phase and 0 at the delimiter, so 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase. The input token is e in 58153 of the 58159 active dev steps (the other 6 are scattered single hits on j, z, q, v and t).

The position claims hold. When the fed-back token is e, the feature never fires at recall_idx 0-1. At recall_idx 2 (e from original position 1) the predicate e & recall_idx==2 has precision 0.055 and only 0.2% of mass. At recall_idx 3 (e from position 2) precision is 0.965 but that bin carries only 11.6% of mass, which fits the claim of weak activations there. At recall_idx >= 4 precision is 1.000 and mass is 88%.

The misses on the test split are 925 steps holding 0.2% of mass. They are all very weak activations (0.01-0.12 of max) on e copied back from original position 1. This is the expected low-magnitude tail, not a separate pattern.

The false positives on the test split are 595 steps, all e from original position 2 (recall_idx 3) where the feature stays at zero. This matches the claim that position 2 gives weak or marginal activation.

The predicate never fires during incorrect copying: e & recall_idx>=3 & correct==0 matches 0 steps, so the model's own mistakes are not a confound. Repeated e (in_count>=2) gives the same precision (0.989), so repetition does not change anything.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim.
